requirement_text.REQ-154: In-band instruction budget for Lua script execution (LUA-08 layer 1). ACs: (1) configurable budget, test drives two budgets; (2) while-true terminates; (3) structured {:error, {:budget_exceeded, limit}} pattern-matched by test; (4) pcall-catches-budget test matches REQ-148 spike OQ-2(a); (5-6) moduledoc content; (7) mix test/compile pass.

acceptance_criteria: the instruction budget is configurable (not a hardcoded literal) and a test drives two different configured budgets and asserts the smaller one halts a loop sooner
a test runs an unbounded while true do end loop under a configured budget and asserts the execution terminates rather than hanging
budget exhaustion surfaces as a structured error value distinguishable by pattern match from other failure arms
a test asserts what a script that pcalls its own budget exhaustion does (expected {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}} per REQ-148 spike OQ-2(a))
moduledoc: LUA-08 layer-1 restatement, :max_instructions pcall-catchable, REQ-155 mandatory layer 2
moduledoc: INV-2 and INV-4 non-port with reasons
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass

task.description: Gate the test spec at test/specs/REQ-154.md and the existing tests in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs against REQ-154 acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Every runnable AC has a named test (module + describe + test name) that would catch a regression
AC-4: test asserts {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}} -- consistent with REQ-148 spike OQ-2(a)
AC-5 and AC-6: spec documents that moduledoc content is verifiable by source read
No skipped or pending tests for covered ACs

summary.AC-1: PASS - Letflow.Engine.Lua.ExecutorTest > instruction budget (REQ-154) > AC-1: smaller budget halts sooner than larger budget on the same loop. Drives max_instructions: 500 (asserts {:error, {:budget_exceeded, 500}}) and max_instructions: 50000 (asserts {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}}) for for i = 1, 5000 do end. Budget is a call-site keyword arg via Keyword.fetch!(opts, :max_instructions). No @tag :skip.
summary.AC-2: PASS - test AC-2: while true do end terminates with budget_exceeded rather than hanging asserts {:error, {:budget_exceeded, 1000}}. Successful assertion proves VM interrupted the loop (hang = ExUnit timeout failure).
summary.AC-3: PASS - test AC-3: budget_exceeded is a structured error, not a bare string or atom matches {:error, {:budget_exceeded, _limit}} = result. Strictly more specific than {:error, _}; cannot be satisfied by {:error, string} or {:error, :invalid_script_ref}.
summary.AC-4: PASS - test AC-4: pcall-caught budget exhaustion returns {:ok, _} -- layer-1 pcall-catchable asserts {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}} for a script wrapping an infinite loop in pcall. Matches REQ-148 spike OQ-2(a): pcall catches, Lua.eval!/2 returns normally, hash computed.
summary.AC-5: PASS - verified by direct source read of lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex @moduledoc. All required phrases present: restates LUA-08 as layer 1 of a two-layer pair; :max_instructions is an in-band pcall-catchable budget; LUA-08 literal MUST terminate not met by this layer alone; Layer 2 (REQ-155) supplies the mandatory host-enforced non-catchable kill via Process.exit/2 on a monitored Task.
summary.AC-6: PASS - verified by direct source read of lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex @moduledoc. INV-2: INV-2 does not port because the threat it guarded against does not exist in this runtime (:max_instructions wired into VM at construction, not reachable from Lua globals; _G.__limiter__ = nil bypass is impossible). INV-4: INV-4 does not port because this runtime has no hook API and needs none (tv-labs/lua enforces :max_instructions via its own internal VM counter).
summary.AC-7: PASS (deferred to TEST-RUNNER as specified) - mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors output to be quoted by TEST-RUNNER.
